original_text: §Constraints — 10 flat bullets, 202 w, mixing hard rules, definitions and implementation contracts

changes: Longest block in the folder and the most skimmed. Three different kinds of statement carry identical weight, so the four things a builder must never break are visually indistinguishable from settled detail. For human readers this is the pacing problem: 200 words of unbroken bold-lead bullets with no table, callout or grouping in the whole SPEC. ~0 words

original_text: design-reference §Deltas from the first render — all four bullets (59 w)

Every delta is already recorded where the builder checks it, so the section is pure restatement — and keeping it is what makes the frame inventories read as revision history instead of target state. Saves 59 words. Alternative if this file doubles as the design's change record: keep §Deltas and instead strip the inline "(removed in the saved revision)" / "(only in the dark frame — …)" annotations (saves 17)

original_text: data-model §Scope closing paragraph — "The current `GET /api/sessions` narrows to `created_by` only; … Reads still use the service-role client after the staff assertion." (27 w)

original_text: Minor, rolled up: "No scheduling." in §Constraints duplicates §Non-goals bullet 1; §Constraints "No aggregate table, materialized view, cron or stored status" already subsumes data-model.md's "No aggregate table or cached rollup" and "Never persist the result"; CAP-5's success criterion restates §Constraints "Creation keeps today's behaviour" timing; `sessions.figcraft` appears bare in §Constraints and as a full path in the companion; CAP-1…CAP-6 carry no inbound reference from any constraint or query section
revised_text: CONDENSE each: drop the duplicate scheduling clause; let SPEC's no-aggregate line be the single statement of the rule; shrink the creation constraint to endpoint + public-attendance; use the full asset path once; either cite the CAP ids from data-model's query sections or stop numbering
changes: Six small duplicate-or-dangling items; any one is trivial, together ≈24 words and several small stumbles. N further minor fixes; ask to expand.

original_text: SPEC CAP-4: "attendance by session, weekly check-ins, top sessions and sessions with no check-ins" and "the attention card lists only in-range sessions with zero check-ins"; Assumptions defines the attention card as "sessions with zero check-ins"; data-model: "Needs attention — in-range sessions with zero attendance"
revised_text: Name each card once, as the design does: "attendance by session, Attendance trend (weekly check-ins), Top sessions, Needs attention (sessions with no check-ins)", then reuse those names: "the `Needs attention` card lists only in-range sessions with zero check-ins"; Assumptions identifies the same card; data-model keeps `Needs attention`
changes: One card answers to four names (weekly check-ins, attendance trend, attention card, Needs attention) and one condition to three (no check-ins, zero check-ins, zero attendance). A builder reconciling SPEC, design and data model cannot tell how many figures exist. Keeps the four-item list and its terse colon form.

original_text: SPEC Success signal: "A session left open across its `attendance_closes_at` flips to `Completed` without a manual write."
revised_text: "A page left open across a session's `attendance_closes_at` shows that session as `Completed` without a manual write."
changes: "A session left open" also describes an attendance window left open — which is exactly what the creation flow does. `data-model.md` means the browser page ("an open page flips `Live now` → `Completed`"). Only the subject is wrong; the behaviour stated is unchanged.

original_text: SPEC Constraints: "**Scope reuses the staff gate.** Admin sees the programme; Preacher sees sessions where they are the owning preacher; Assistant sees their assigned preacher's." and "after the staff assertion"; data-model Scope: "the spec widens a Preacher to their owned sessions"
revised_text: "**Scope reuses the existing staff authorization check.** Admin sees the programme; a Preacher sees the sessions where they are the named preacher; an Assistant sees their assigned preacher's sessions." / "after that check" / "the spec widens a Preacher's scope to the sessions they own"
changes: "Gate", "assertion" and `getStaffContext()` name one step three ways, and "gate" is a metaphor the document never introduces. "Owning preacher" and "owned sessions" are coined here and defined nowhere. "Their assigned preacher's" ends on a possessive with no noun; "widens a Preacher" widens a person rather than a scope. No authorization rule changes.

original_text: SPEC CAP-5: "its attendance link is available"; Constraints: "and enables public attendance"
revised_text: "its public attendance link (`/attend?session=<id>`) is available"; "and enables the public attendance link"
changes: Both terms arrive before anything defines them; the contract names the route only on the last line of `data-model.md`. Naming it at first use keeps SPEC.md readable alone — the same route the contract already fixes, not a new one.

original_text: SPEC CAP-5: "submitting it creates a session with attendance open now and closing at now + duration"
revised_text: "submitting it creates a session whose attendance opens at that moment and closes at `now + duration_minutes`"
changes: "With attendance open now" parses as the current state — attendance is open now — rather than the opening event the Constraints describe. "now + duration" is also a third notation alongside `duration_minutes` and "name, location, duration".

original_text: SPEC CAP-6: "a side-by-side check against `design-reference.md` matches layout, type, spacing and tokens."
revised_text: "a side-by-side comparison with `design-reference.md` shows matching layout, type, spacing and tokens."
changes: The subject of "matches" is "a check", and a check is not what matches the design. Same requirement, same words otherwise.

original_text: SPEC Why: "The design set gives Sessions…"; Open Questions: "The saved design no longer contains…"; Constraints: "**Design authority** is `sessions.figcraft`"; design-reference: "Authority: …" and "the light frame dropped it in the saved revision"
revised_text: Introduce it once — "the saved design (`sessions.figcraft`)" — then "the saved design" throughout; keep "Authority:" in the companion as a heading-level pointer
changes: Five names for one artifact: design set, the design, the saved design, the saved revision, design authority. A reader cannot tell whether the design set and the saved revision are the same thing, or which one is normative when they disagree.

original_text: data-model: "Missing email renders `—`; the design's `priya.raman@gmail.com` is sample data."; design-reference frames: "48 sessions · folk programme", "Weekend Camp 2026", "42 of 60", "Sep 2025"

original_text: SPEC CAP-1: "an empty programme renders the designed empty state"; CAP-3: "selecting one shows the designed record with phone, email…"
revised_text: "renders the empty state specified in `design-reference.md`"; "shows the record specified in `design-reference.md`"

original_text: SPEC Open Questions: "The saved design no longer contains a desktop `Session detail` frame. Restore it, or is desktop limited to Overview and Reports?"; "…there is no capacity or invite data. Add an expected-attendees field, or show totals only?"; "or keep the current inline form on `/sessions`?"
revised_text: "Should the desktop `Session detail` frame be restored, or is desktop limited to Overview and Reports?"; "Should an expected-attendees field be added, or should the report show totals only?"; "…or should `/sessions` keep the current inline form?"
changes: Each pairs an imperative with an interrogative, so it is unclear whether the reader is told to act or asked to decide. The third also shifts subject from `New session` to an unnamed keeper of the form. Apply wherever the section lands; "under-filled sessions" is also a state the design never shows — consider "sessions below the shown capacity".

original_text: SPEC Why: "Sessions is where the programme records who actually came, but today `/sessions` is a live check-in manager: staff start a session, watch the attendance dashboard, and the record then leaves their view."
revised_text: Consider: "The Sessions module is where the programme records who actually came, but today `/sessions` is only a live check-in screen: staff start a session, watch the attendance dashboard, and then the record leaves their view."
changes: "Manager" reads as a staff role in a document that names three roles two sections later. "Sessions" arrives as a bare plural before the module name is established. The third item in a list of staff actions is an outcome, not an action. The "record leaves their view" image is worth keeping.

original_text: data-model Edge cases: "Attendance links stay the existing `/attend?session=<id>` route; the overview exposes the link for a Live session only."
revised_text: "Attendance links use the existing `/attend?session=<id>` route; the overview exposes the link only while the session reads `Live now`."
changes: "A Live session" reads as a fourth status beside `Upcoming`, `Live now` and `Completed`; the token is the one that exists. "Stay" describes the document, not the link.

original_text: SPEC CAP-3: "an attendee's full contact record"; Constraints: "the attendee record joins `contacts`"; data-model: "Contact record for…" (the panel clause goes with the structure pass); Edge cases: "the contact panel always resolves"
revised_text: "contact record" in all four places; Edge cases: "the contact record is always found"
changes: One surface, four names. "Resolves" is jargon for "is found". The record joins `contacts`, so "contact record" is the accurate term — "attendee record" implies a second entity.

original_text: SPEC CAP-1: "attendee total"; Constraints: "**Attendance total** is the count of `attendance` rows for the session"; Success signal: "the correct headcount"; design-reference: "attendee total"

original_text: SPEC CAP-3: "first contact, sessions attended and last attended"; data-model: "first contact (`contacts.created_at`)"
revised_text: "first contact date (`contacts.created_at`)"

original_text: design-reference: "The saved design removed `Open`, `Draft` and `Scheduled`; there is no manual status."
revised_text: "The saved design removed the `Open`, `Draft` and `Scheduled` statuses; there is no manual status."

revised_text: "primary button `+ New session`" in all three; "moon and logout icons right"; "The design builder is `build_sessions_designs.py`" or leave the script bare, and "Campaign design-builder tokens"

original_text: SPEC "## Open Questions"; "The reports totals match a direct count of `attendance`…"; data-model "(virtualised table)"; SPEC CAP-5 "without leaving the sessions flow" vs Why "without leaving the module"
revised_text: "## Open questions"; "The report totals match…"; "(virtualized table)"; "without leaving the module"
changes: Four small fixes: the only title-case heading among sentence-case siblings; "reports totals" reads as a missing possessive for a single figure; the corpus mixes -ise and -ize ("materialized view" in Constraints, "virtualised" here) and Microsoft style asks for -ize; "flow" and "module" name the same container, and "flow" also names the whole document.
